Market today: The mood is mixed. Nvidia's strong earnings are a bright spot for chips, but the S&P 500 just broke crucial support, signaling broader market weakness. Geopolitical tensions and new US-China tech rules add headwinds for your concentrated tech/chip book.

Your holdings: Most of your book is flashing "SELL," with several leveraged ETFs like SOXL (-78.17%), MUU (-61.79%), and SMCI (-44.99%) showing massive drawdowns. Trading on margin amplifies these drops, making risk management critical. CRWD (+25.52%) is a strong performer marked "TRIM."

Watch: Keep an eye on the S&P 500's reaction to its broken support level and any further developments on US-China tech regulations. The upcoming Fed minutes could also move the market.

Bottom line: Prioritize aggressive risk management and consider reducing exposure, especially in leveraged and deeply negative positions.
plays: Trim CRWD: Take some profit on CRWD (+25.52%) given its "TRIM" status and the broader market weakness.
Review leveraged "SELL" positions: Consider trimming into any strength on SOXL (-78.17%), MUU (-61.79%), and SMCI (-44.99%) to reduce margin risk.
Consider a hedge: With the S&P 500 breaking support, look at SOXS (semiconductor bear 3X) as a potential hedge. Scanner entry 58.71-58.65, stop 58.16.
